name: Neistra v0.39.0
body:
Neistra v0.39.0 adds a ligand information sidebar for deliberate inspection of an entry and its exact ligand instance. It combines cached 2D depiction, current molecular properties, sourced profile comparisons, and an accessible radar with an equivalent values/limits table.

- Choose or clear the inspected entry independently of molecular selection and visibility. Repeated ligand instances keep their exact identity and automatic/manual origin.
- Edits, previews, Undo/Redo, and source failures retire incompatible values, formula, depiction and comparisons. Missing results, unavailable chemistry and clipped axes have explicit states; radar area is not a scientific score.
- Collapse, resize and reopen the sidebar across desktop and narrow layouts. Connected reading position and focus are preserved as compatible results arrive.
- Existing inspection/editing tools remain available. Entry-property filtering follows in #162; general Inspector retirement follows in #163.

This additive minor release keeps database head `0017`, archive version 3 and viewer version 2. All five authoritative versions are 0.39.0; dependencies and scientific methods are unchanged. Uploaded originals and existing database history remain compatible. Archives retain their existing canonical snapshot semantics, including the documented omission of command history.

[PR #183](https://github.com/ManuelSe/Neistra/pull/183) merged normally at `e3fd5858763dfa37520b8d812e6df30d9c031a3d`. Its complete tree equals reviewed feature head `ebdc43ad8532adccf62a04ea171ad76fd31f1317`. All seven specialist agents returned final PASS on that feature head. These are specialist agent assessments, not human approvals; the requested automated PR review returned no assessment.

Both the clean candidate and the exact merged commit completed all 43 qualification commands with normal outer exit 0, followed by successful terminal finalization, strict summary and strong retention. Each records 4,266 Python passes with zero skips, 2,090 frontend passes, 14 supervisor passes, and 641 browser passes with the same 75 approved exclusions and zero failures/flakes/retries. All 1,222 selected source/helper/configuration/fixture bodies and six DATA bodies remain exact. Actual v0.38.0 source-bound producers/readers pass both directions and archive suffixes. Independent merged source/closure/raw/archive/deployment, scientific/reader/resource, performance, UI and UX readbacks pass.

Timing remains diagnostic under the portable policy: the merged run misses 142 of 410 actual property/profile targets, compared with 143 in the candidate run. Four additional missed annotations are synthetic policy controls and are excluded from these workload counts. All four merged bulk active-readiness samples exceed five seconds: desktop repeated/distinct 7,578.8/8,367.4 ms and compact 5,044.4/6,441.0 ms. Primary-only RSS, browser/GPU peaks and simultaneous total memory are unavailable. No strict-host timing, speedup, regression-causation, physical-device or screen-reader qualification is claimed; cancellation observations do not establish hidden-retirement or sole-worker termination latency.

Required qualification parts, finite context, original failure histories and literal checksums accompany the release. Earlier failed campaigns remain failures and do not count as successful qualification. Final publication/download verification is recorded separately in the delivery receipt and issue reply; the runtime tag remains immutable.

Interaction-diagram generation remains #153; its exact-instance/revision boundary reports unavailable. #164/#165 and the parent program's other exclusions are unchanged.

Refs #161. Refs #11. Parent #11 remains open for the complete required program.
